title: The liver makes bile, which helps digest fats, and the gallbladder stores it
summary: On the NIDDK digestion page, bile from the liver helps with fats and some vitamins, and the gallbladder holds it between meals.
body: Bile is the liver's secretion on the NIDDK page last reviewed in December 2017. The page gives it one digestive job: help with fats and some vitamins. Ducts can park it in the gallbladder, which keeps it between meals, or send it onward for use. At a meal the gallbladder squeezes the stored bile out. The page stops at that help. It does not explain how fat droplets come apart. The text is a public-domain NIH description.

sources.title: Your Digestive System & How it Works
sources.author: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
sources.note: US NIH page. Public domain. Paraphrased. Supports the bile and gallbladder sentences.
